steps.evidence: Data was pre-processed through probabilistic quotient normalisation (PQN) normalisation using MetaX
quality control-based robust locally estimated scatterplot smoothing signal correction and removal of metabolites with high coefficient variation (> 30%)
Using vegan R package, sample-wise variation between metabolite treatment groups was assessed using Principal Coordinates Analysis (PCOA) based on Euclidean distances
differences in global metabolite composition were tested using permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) at 999 permutations
Using MetaboAnalystR, we applied Mummichog, GSEA (Gene Set Enrichment Analysis), as well as their combined approach.
We adopted a tolerance of 5 ppm while using the Gallus gallus gene set as background (cut-off threshold set at 0.05).

Functional analyses were based on significant differences between the metabolite peak values of T1 and T2 that were assessed by student sample t-test and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, for parametric and non-parametric data distributions, respectively, using base R.
KEGG pathways were further mapped using R package Pathview
We further applied the sparse partial least squares discriminant analysis (sPLS-DA) algorithm on our PQN-normalised data from the mixOmics package to perform feature selection
This information was subjected to chemical class enrichment using basic ChemRICH analysis
We also employed ChemRICH class enrichment analysis of the same features, but with classification based on the ChemOnt system via the ClassyFire program.

We applied the Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker discovery using Latent cOmponents (DIABLO) method from the mixOmics package, to determine the correlation between our metabolome and MAG datasets.

A design matrix with a link set at 0.10 (based on the recommendation of the original authors of mixOmics, this value represents a reasonable trade-off between discrimination, i.e., T1 and T2, and correlations across metagenomics and metabolomic datasets) was used to discriminate features between the treatment groups.
The validity of the DIABLO models was then confirmed by a permutation test, comparing CERs of the original model to those generated by randomly permuted samples (p < 0.05).
From the model, moderate correlations between MAGs and metabolites of at least 0.60 were retained
and thereafter subjected to pairwise comparison with Benjamini-Hochberg p-value correction (p < 0.05).

Both significant and non-significant correlation counts, CV stability values, and selected metabolic module features of significant MAGs were mapped together using the ComplexHeatMap package for complete clustering analysis based on the Euclidean method.
Correlations between significant MAGs and metabolites based on DIABLO, with further evidence based on sPLS-DA, were also drawn using the igraph package.
